threat_internal_label: people using a cloned voice to mislead voters (never shown on screen)
analog: AI voice-clone robocalls telling New Hampshire voters not to vote, Jan 21, 2024, two days before the state's presidential primary
actors_note: The red is people's choices: a political consultant commissioned a cloned voice and paid a robocall firm to send it; a carrier signed the calls as trustworthy without checking. The voice tool is not the actor. On screen: no real politician's likeness or voice, no party cues; a gray phone rings, a hand chose to send it.

sources.title: FCC 24-59, Notice of Apparent Liability against Steve Kramer (May 2024) - Voice Broadcasting 'initiated 9,581 calls on January 21, 2024'; two days before the primary; proposed $6,000,000
NPR: New Hampshire is investigating a robocall that was made to sound like Biden (Jan 22, 2024) - AG: message 'appears to be artificially generated', an 'unlawful attempt to disrupt' the primary

New Hampshire DOJ: Voter Suppression AI Robocall Investigation Update (Feb 6, 2024) - tracebacks via the Industry Traceback Group identified Life Corporation and originating provider Lingo Telecom; cease-and-desist issued; Anti-Robocall Multistate Litigation Task Force (50 AGs) and FCC Enforcement Bureau
FCC: FCC Makes AI-Generated Voices in Robocalls Illegal (declaratory ruling, Feb 8, 2024, effective immediately)
Wiley: FCC and FTC Launch Inquiries on AI and Voice Cloning - FCC Notice of Inquiry on AI and robocalls released Nov 16, 2023 (FCC 23-101), including whether AI calls could disrupt elections
Pindrop: Pindrop Reveals TTS Engine Behind Biden AI Robocall (analysis published Jan 25, 2024; 39-second clip scored in 155 segments of 250 ms)
NPR: Criminal charges and FCC fines issued for deepfake Biden robocalls (May 23, 2024)
CyberScoop: FCC wants major telecoms to step up rules around AI-generated robocalls - Lingo signed the calls with an 'A-level' STIR/SHAKEN attestation, the highest trust level
FCC: Lingo Telecom settlement, $1 million (announced Aug 21, 2024), via Slashdot/FCC reporting
Fortune: FCC bans AI-generated robocalls (Feb 8, 2024); FCC chair proposed the ruling Jan 31, 2024 (per law-firm summaries)

points.event: 9,581 calls initiated on Jan 21 (all within day 0)

events.event: Jan 23: primary election; the red's window closes

threat.notes: extent = share of the 9,581 calls counted by the FCC (s1). All were placed on one day; the hour-by-hour spread was not found, so draw them as a single-day burst. Some reports give higher estimates of call volume; the FCC's count is used. Measurable effect on turnout was not established by any source found; don't imply one.

fragments.had: an open inquiry into AI voices in robocalls, including the election risk
fragments.notes: Notice of Inquiry released Nov 16, 2023, 66 days before t0

fragments.had: a way to vouch for or flag who is really calling
fragments.notes: the June 30, 2021 compliance deadline (935 days before t0) is well known but was not seen in a snippet. The originating carrier signed these calls 'A-level' anyway (s8): the check existed and was not applied.

fragments.had: the ability to trace a call back hop by hop to its source
fragments.notes: existed before t0 (founding date not verified); in other cases it has traced calls in about an hour (congressional testimony, not verified here)

fragments.who: voters who got the call, and the state attorney general's election unit
fragments.had: the recordings and the authority to warn the public
fragments.notes: public warning on Jan 22, the day before the vote

fragments.who: a voice-security firm's deepfake audio detector
fragments.had: proof the voice was synthetic, and which engine made it
the legal lever: declare AI voices 'artificial' under existing robocall law
fragments.notes: proposed Jan 31 (t=10), adopted unanimously Feb 8 (t=18, s4)

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented dates, not a measured distribution: p10 = AG's public warning Jan 22 (t=1, s2), which did land before the vote; median = source traced and cease-and-desist issued Feb 6 (t=16, s3); p90 = criminal charges and the $6M proposed fine, May 23 (t=123, s1/s7). The carrier settlement came Aug 21, 2024 (t=213, s9).

deploy.notes: Feb 8, 2024: declaratory ruling effective immediately, making cloned-voice robocalls without consent illegal nationwide.

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative. One person used a cloned voice to mislead; the counterfactual is defenders using AI to connect what they already held. (1) Scoring a 39-second clip as synthetic is a seconds-to-minutes machine task (a detector did it, published at t=4, s6); (2) sorting incoming voter complaints, matching them to the same spoofed number, and opening a traceback request is routing work well inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry), cheap to run continuously given RATES.md's ~40x/yr cost fall (Epoch). Assumed ~1 day to source traced and carrier told to stop, i.e. before the primary at t=2, versus the human 16 days. Subpoenas, charges and rulings stay human and are not sped up. The public warning already landed at t=1 by human effort, so the gain is in tracing and stopping, not warning. Not a claim any vote would have changed.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: 9,581 cloned-voice calls went out in one day, two days before the vote; a warning came next day, but tracing the sender took 16 days and charges 123, though the tracing network, call authentication and an FCC inquiry all existed beforehand.
